newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofwat calls for improved accounting methods.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofwat calls for improved accounting methods.

text.p: UK water industry regulator Ofwat said on Tuesday it wanted companies to improve accounting procedures through more competitive tendering and reporting on indirect transactions with associates.

In a statement, Ofwat head Ian Byatt said he had "some concerns about a situation where trade with associates is a high proportion of the turnover...and where the associates are heavily dependent upon trade with the regulated business."
He suggested that in those cases, it might be preferrable to reintegrate the associate into the core business.
Byatt's remarks came in tandem with publication of Ofwat's report on "Transfer Pricing in the Water Industry."
Ofwat said that checks under the study had revealed "a number of areas where the regulator wants to see changes," adding that all companies involved had agreed to remedy practices.

Byatt acknowledged that it was not the regulator's job to audit company procedures but he added that the reviews "have shown the need for improved scrutiny of company compliance in this area by their auditors."
